doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Tonight Show music heard on air and the Donte's gig
summary: Viewers heard only fragments of the band's playing; at Donte's the band hit a third page it had never played.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Does it ever get frustrating? Some of your music, the T.V. audience must have heard the first ten seconds and the last five seconds, you know? That always bugged me.
The band would start out and it sounds so great—

Well if you were in the studio, you heard a lot of music. You can tell it by how many commercials, because we played through all the commercials. Unfortunately, out over the air it only came the last ten or fifteen seconds.
Yeah. In fact, you know what happened?
We used to be on the air for a minute at midnight every night, and then they took that away and filled that up with commercials.

Yeah. We played a gig at Donte’s in L.A. one time. It was a jazz joint. And it was the whole Tonight Show band and I was in front. And we were playing the same arrangements, but when we were playing the jobs we’d get to the third page, which we never had got to that.
Some guys never saw that page.
That’s where it disintegrated. I don’t know whether it was that they couldn’t read, or I think it was the shock of the thing, you know?
That’s funny. That’s funny. You expect someone to say “okay, cut.”
That’s right. Nobody to save you.
